title: Coupon email → purchase
teaser: Starts as a clean A/B test; higher levels add CRM cherry-picking and opens.
question: Did our 20%-off coupon email actually make people buy?
ask: We want the extra purchases per 100 customers emailed.

outcome.name: purchased_30d
outcome.meaning: 1 = made a purchase within 30 days of send day

variables.name: orders_last_year
variables.meaning: orders in the 12 months before send day

post_treatment.name: site_visits_30d
post_treatment.meaning: site visits in the 30 days after send

notes.text: The email went to a random half of the list.
It was meant to be a random half, but the CRM team also added customers they thought were likely to respond.
The CRM team hand-picked who got it based on what customers had been browsing that week; that browsing data wasn't kept.
Only people who were sent the email can open it.

traps.name: Consequence column
traps.text: opened_email only exists for recipients and tracks buyers; controlling for it distorts the answer.

traps.name: Cherry-picking on past behaviour
traps.text: The CRM team added likely responders; plain comparison overstates.

traps.name: Unrecorded intent
traps.text: Selection on unrecorded browsing intent; not answerable from this file.
